name: Borgo Pignano
insider_take: This 18th-century villa sits on a 750-acre organic farm where Chianina cattle roam freely and ancient olive groves produce award-winning extra virgin olive oil.
whats_special: Borgo Pignano operates as a completely self-sustaining estate with its own organic farm, vineyard, and even a truffle hunting ground. The property features original frescoes by renowned Italian artists and houses one of Tuscany's most impressive private art collections. Guests can participate in the olive harvest each October and witness the traditional pressing process in the estate's 200-year-old frantoio.
pro_tip: Book the "Truffle Hunter for a Day" experience during peak season (November-December) – the estate's trained dogs have an exceptional success rate finding the prized white truffles that can sell for thousands per pound.
dont_miss: The sunrise hot air balloon rides launching directly from the estate's grounds offer unparalleled views of the Val d'Elsa valley. Also visit the property's restored 13th-century chapel where Gregorian chants echo during weekly evening services, and explore the underground wine cellars carved into volcanic rock formations dating back to Etruscan times.
pros: Stunning 18th-century villa estate with authentic Tuscan charm
Panoramic views of rolling Tuscan hills and vineyards
Comprehensive wellness center with spa treatments and yoga pavilion
Sustainable luxury with organic gardens and eco-friendly practices
cons: Remote countryside location requires rental car for area exploration
Premium pricing reflects luxury estate positioning
